failing_job_findings.cause: CodSpeed reports test_get_state_uncached[disk] regressed from 56.5 ms to 70.1 ms (-19.39% efficiency), while warning that base and head used different runtime environments. The PR deliberately adds one asyncio.to_thread hop to uncached disk-state reads so filesystem I/O no longer blocks the event loop; the author attributes the measured single-benchmark slowdown to that intended thread hop.

The Ubuntu 3.12 job log shows both setup and the first 10,515-test pass succeeded. The second unit-test pass reached 87% before GitHub cancelled the job at the workflow's configured 30-minute timeout; no assertion failed. unit-tests-gate then failed only because unit-tests=cancelled.

outstanding_asks.ask: Re-run the cancelled Ubuntu 3.12 unit-test job and decide whether to accept the expected disk cache-miss CodSpeed regression.

CodSpeed flags `test_get_state_uncached[disk]` at −19% on 8e22f9e (58.2 → 72 ms). The other 146 benchmarks show no regression. The slowdown comes from what this PR is for, not from a leftover bug. On a cache miss, `StateManagerDisk.get_state` now reads the session's pickles in a worker thread so file I/O no longer blocks the event loop. - **Before 7ac5e9c:** each substate took its own thread hop, about twice main's cost (+102%). - **Since 7ac5e9c:** the whole tree is read in one `asyncio.to_thread` call, so what's left is the cost of that single hop. - **Measured:** callgrind puts an uncached `get_state` on the benchmark tree at about 761k–778k instructions, against 633k on main.
